title: Test and CI speed. Goal: cut PR CI wall time and local test time sharply; planner decides every deferred point. Evidence (PR #2 run 22, `.github/workflows/pr.yml`): critical path is `wails-linux-cli` (1.5 min) then `checks (Linux)` (4 min, `typecheck` alone 1 min 50 s) then `ui` and `container-tests` in parallel (10 min and 9 min); `ui` and `container-tests` `needs` all three check jobs, so they idle until lint, typecheck and macOS finish. `test:ui:studio` took ~8 min before failing, and the `ipc-frontend` and `visual` steps run serially after it in the same job. `container-tests`: `docker load` of the cached image tar ~80 s, Go tests ~5.5 min, `test:unit` 12 s. Every Linux job repeats `apt-get install` of GTK4/WebKitGTK (~30 s), `setup-go` (~20 s) and `bun install`. Scope (1) CI: remove needless `needs` edges so test jobs start at once; split `ipc-frontend` and `visual` into own jobs; shard Playwright (`--shard`) across runners; cache the apt packages, the Go build and test cache and the Playwright browsers; avoid the `docker load` tar (pull in parallel, or smaller images); share one setup via a composite action instead of copy-pasted steps (workflow edits go through `docs/pending-workflows/`, see `docs/DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md`). (2) Tests: measure per-spec and per-package duration (Playwright JSON reporter, `go test -json`), list the slowest, then fix causes: fixed sleeps and long timeouts, `retries`, serial `workers: 1` projects, per-test app/DB/container setup that can be shared, duplicate coverage between flow tests and UI specs, `-count` or `-race` overuse, Testcontainers started per test not per package. Split a fast default tier from the slow tier where a test cannot be made fast. (3) This box: check why local runs are slow (4 cores, 15 GB; Playwright `workers: '100%'`, Docker, `build:test:studio` rebuilt on every run, cold Go and bun caches, hooks running the whole suite) and fix or document in `docs/DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md`. Record before and after timings in the plan result. Decline nothing silently: name each rejected option and its reason.
status: Done (CI half pending the pr.yml patch)

Git hooks scope to changed files; pre-commit is 0.5s for docs-only, 0.1s for Go-only and 56s for studio frontend commits, and pre-push for a Go-only range runs tests of the changed package.
Frontend commits get no hook speedup because the lint rules take 17s and the changed projects must typecheck.
The Ryuk image is not pulled because the go-containers job sets TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true.

TestImageRegistryURL failed because a plain alpine:3.20 tag (from a manual pull/tag recipe) made the registry-link logic pick the implied Hub name; with that tag removed the test passes unchanged. It was not a containerd-store issue.

CI estimates, not measured: run wall time drops from 15m47s to about 6 min warm (about 60% less), while billed Linux runner-minutes stay about equal (24.9 before, 23.8 after); cold-cache runs add about 1.5 min per job.

title: Release flow speed; publish, not draft. Goal: cut tag-to-release wall time and publish the release directly. Evidence (`.github/workflows/release.yml`, trigger `push` of tags `v*.*.*`): jobs `test-matrix` and `db-compat` (ubuntu, timeouts 30 and 60 min) run first, then `release` (macos-15, `needs` both, timeout 60 min) builds, signs and packages and ends in a `gh release create --draft` step (~line 213). Recent runs take ~15 to 31 min (run 10: 31 min; run 11 for tag `v0.2.6` was still running at 18 min). Scope (1) Speed: measure per-job and per-step times from the last successful release runs (GitHub Actions API); remove duplicate work against the PR workflow (the tagged commit already passed PR CI: decide whether `test-matrix` and `db-compat` must rerun on a tag at all, or can be replaced by a check that the commit's PR checks passed); start the macOS build in parallel with the tests and gate only the publish step on them; reuse the setup action and caches from P294 (`.github/actions/setup`, Go build cache, bun cache); avoid rebuilding what PR CI built. (2) Publish: the release is created already published, not draft, but only after the tests pass and the assets are uploaded and verified (create it as the last step, or upload to a draft and publish in a final step; planner decides). (3) Failure safety: a failed gate must not leave a published release; state how a bad tag is handled. Workflow edits go through `docs/pending-changes/` (see `docs/DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md`). Record before and after timings. Name each rejected option and its reason.
lines: The release workflow .github/workflows/release.yml triggers on push of tags v*.*.*, runs jobs test-matrix and db-compat (ubuntu, timeouts 30 and 60 min) first, then the release job (macos-15, needs both, timeout 60 min) which builds, signs and packages.

Workflow edits must go through docs/pending-changes/ (see docs/DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md), so the release.yml change is delivered as a pending patch to apply.
P295 added a release gate script, scripts/release-ci-gate.sh, which supports --dry-run and has a dispatch path (exit 3 means it would dispatch, exit 1 means a failed run).
The setup action (.github/actions/setup) gained a cache-save option; the cache-save: true branch equals the old steps plus one && clause.
The new publish job fetches the DMGs with gh run download (needs actions: read) instead of actions/download-artifact, because no verified pin for that action was reachable.
release.yml has no dry run, so after-change release timings can only be measured on a real tag.

title: Memory: code comments are plain comments. Decisions final (user, 2026-10-18). The memory tool never touches files and never adds comment markers: `store_memory` `asComment` must not return a marker-wrapped `kira-memory` block (today it returns one: header line plus `km_` fact lines, built by `Service.Prepare`/`commentFor`/`memfmt.FormatComment` from `MarkersFor`; the tool reads no file, only a path or extension to pick the marker). A code comment is a normal comment, not a memory: no `kira-memory` header, no `km_` fact lines, no tags, ids, keywords or provenance of its own. A comment may only reference a memory, by its id; the id always resolves because the memory is stored the normal way. To condense text for a comment the agent uses distill (P297 merges it into memory). Planner decides: what to remove or keep in `internal/memory/memfmt` comment format (`ParseComments`, `FormatComment`, `markers.go`, retired-format messages), `internal/memory/memcheck` and the `memory-check` subcommand (does it still scan comments, and does it check that a reference resolves?), `Service.Prepare`/`PrepareResult`, the `asComment` flag and its MCP schema and texts, prompts in `internal/llmprompts`, the install instructions text, the site `memory-formats` page, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; the exact reference syntax (grep-first, one token, cannot be mistaken for prose); and what happens to comment blocks already in the repo. The `.memory.md` doc format and import write-back stay unchanged in this phase (P297 changes them). Real `claude` rows of `docs/DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md` re-run after prompt changes.

title: Memory: distill collapses into memory; rules. Decisions final (user, 2026-10-18). (1) A memory can be a rule: a standing, general imperative with a reason (`Never write amounts as floats, because the ledger rejects fractions.`), as durable as a fact. Add a `kind` (`fact` or `rule`) to `memories` (migration; versions are immutable, so fixed per version) and no other new metadata. The gate (`memory.gate.system`), the import extract and finalize prompts and the no-challenge mode stop treating an imperative as non-durable: they still refuse one-off tasks and questions, and still require a reason. Planner decides whether `kind` appears in search and MCP outputs (default yes, as a plain word). (2) Distill collapses into memory: one tool. `ingest_files` gains a no-store flag (planner names it) that runs the same pipeline (chunk, extract, verify, finalize merge) and returns the merged lines instead of storing; it also accepts `text`, not only paths. The `distill` MCP tool is removed or kept as a thin alias of that call (planner decides); the UI Distill view and Import as document keep working on the same backend. Today distill chunks and distils each part in an isolated call and only concatenates the lines, so duplicates across parts survive: the merge pass of import's finalize step 1 is shared, not rewritten. With no store the merge covers the input only; the call never reads the store. (3) One mode: the `instructions` mode is removed; the one prompt keeps rules as short imperatives and facts as claims, negations, numbers, units, names, paths and template variables verbatim. (4) Examples: an example is never a memory by itself; it stays inside a rule or fact only when the rule is hard to state without it (an exact command, format or error string), fits on one plain-text line with no backticks, and is stated in the source; anything longer becomes a pointer to the path where it lives; the reason carries the why. (5) Doc format `kira-memory: 3`: top-level `## Facts` and `## Rules`, the source section as `###` under each; fact items stay `- <id> <text>` with the optional indented reason; the `Stated in <from>, <heading>` locator keeps using the source heading, never the category; a missing category means facts or is a reported problem (planner decides, `kira-memory: 2` follows the v1 precedent of one reported problem); update `memfmt` parser, formatter, validator, `writedoc.go`, `memcheck` and the site `memory-formats` page. (6) Outputs of one pipeline: stored memories, merged lines (no store), `.memory.md` doc. Update MCP texts and docs, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, prompts, and re-run the real `claude` rows of `docs/DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md`. Runs after P296.

title: Memory: drop operational trivia from distill and import output. Decisions final (user, 2026-10-18). The extract and merge prompts (shared by import and distill) must not output facts about how a run was executed instead of what was decided or built: refused or conflicting pushes and branch handling, sandbox or environment limits, one-off or flaky test runs and timeouts, fixture or harness gaps noted only to explain a skipped check, what was left for the user to verify, commit mechanics. Decisions with their reasons, constraints, design choices and their consequences stay. Applies to both modes; no use case keeps the trivia. Change goes through the prompts (`memory.merge.system` and the extract prompt), not a filter after the fact. Evidence: `docs/v2.6/plans/P299-pilot/` (v2.0 P131 Part 2 and v1.8 P90 outputs hold such lines). Check: P289-style eval subset round for `R_ess`, `P`, `C_store` against the P297 round (`round-p297-01`) and the P289 baselines, plus a re-run of the same 10 pilot units from `P299-pilot/units.jsonl` counting trivia lines before and after and checking no decision marker is lost; real `claude` rows for gate, distill, import. Report numbers to the user before P299 runs the full pass.
lines: The extract and merge prompts (shared by import and distill) must not output facts about how a run was executed: refused or conflicting pushes, branch handling, sandbox or environment limits, flaky test runs or timeouts, fixture or harness gaps noted to explain a skipped check, what was left for the user to verify, or commit mechanics.
Decisions with their reasons, constraints, design choices and their consequences stay in memory output; the trivia exclusion applies to both import and distill, with no exception.
Trivia removal is done through the prompts (memory.merge.system and the extract prompt), not by a filter after the fact.

In the P298 pilot over 10 units, trivia lines fell from 11 to 4 with the reworded prompts. The model still keeps harness and fixture facts as test knowledge even when the Drop list names them. The user accepted this on 2026-10-18, relaxing the trivia pass line from at most 1.
The reworded prompts removed the push, flake, live-check, baseline, real-phone and install trivia lines from output.
A stronger Drop wording risks losing the pathspec guard, which the reworded prompt lost once in the pilot (P131 Part 2) before it came back on rerun.
With the reworded prompts, eval round p298-01 had R_ess 0.903, R_all 0.769, P 0.562 and unsupported 0.000. P is up 0.041 versus p297-01 and 0.008 under the P289 floor of 0.570.
The holdout doc-devenv-claude lost no environment fact under the reworded prompts, with R_ess 0.958 in both rounds.

The P298 change added the prompt memory.runTrivia and grew memory.import.extract.system from 2852 to 4020 chars, memory.merge.system from 2605 to 3824, and memory.import.finalize.system from 3622 to 4841.

title: Docs history. Decisions final (user, 2026-10-18). Replace every `docs/v*/` chapter except v2.6 (and v2.5 until the eval harness is confirmed not to read `P285-runs`) with one `docs/HISTORY.md`; then delete those chapters' `SPEC.md` and `plans/`. No model reads the old prose: a script builds `HISTORY.md` with zero model tokens. Per phase it keeps the P-number, title, status and first sentence of its SPEC row, plus from that phase's `## P<n> result` section the opening paragraph and every line matching decision markers (decision, decided, user override, declined, rejected, instead of, rather than, supersedes, reverted, renumbered), with a size cap per phase. Prose outside any `P<n>` section is scanned by the same markers and filed under its chapter. The planner measures output size and checks a sample of phases against their source so a decision found only elsewhere in a SPEC is caught. Code comments and docs pointing at `docs/v*/plans/...` are repointed at `HISTORY.md` or lose the reference. Git history keeps the deleted files.

title: Docs history, v2.5 and the tool fix. Decisions final (user, 2026-10-18). v2.5 is done and folds into `docs/HISTORY.md` like P299 did. Order inside the phase: (1) `scripts/docshistory` `repoint` must skip its own files (`scripts/docshistory/`), so a fold no longer rewrites the tool's test fixtures; (2) move what the memory eval harness reads at runtime out of `docs/v2.5/plans/` (P285 and P291 corpora, run folders, the `promptsizes` default path, every other runtime reader the planner finds) to a non-docs location, keeping the harness green and the baselines comparable; (3) fold v2.5 with the CLAUDE.md rollover command (distill via `ingest_files`, sequential `--jobs 1`, rate-limit backoff), verify sample, repoint, `git rm` the v2.5 folder except what moved; (4) drop `docs/WEBVIEW-SCROLL-MEMORY.md` (user: stale): delete it, fix every reference (code comments in `internal/shell`, `wkhost.swift`, `columns.ts`, `budgets.spec.ts`, `perfProbe.ts`; `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md`, `PERF.md`) to a `git show <commit>:docs/WEBVIEW-SCROLL-MEMORY.md` pointer or drop the reference where it no longer helps, and remove the tool's special-case for it in `repoint.go`; (5) update CLAUDE.md and DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md for the moved data. Normal loop: Opus plan first, then Sonnet implementer. Cost: the plan states a projected figure from the P299 mean (0.068 USD per phase) and the v2.5 unit count; the orchestrator confirms with the user if it passes 10 USD. docs/v2.6 stays.

title: E2E coverage for the P301 editor fixes. Decisions final (user, 2026-10-18). Two end-to-end tests, each split at the IPC boundary per CLAUDE.md (backend flow test asserts the result, frontend UI spec asserts the same result): (1) finding 1.1: a workflow YAML or step-editor route that sends back to a manual or skipped step is refused (parser error), and the editor hides those steps in the route options while keeping the current pick visible; (2) finding 1.2: removing, moving, changing the kind of, or toggling the smart script of a step clears a stale `review.implementer`, and the next save succeeds. title: Distill the standing docs: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (600 KB), `docs/PACKAGING.md` (43 KB), `docs/HUMAN_CODE_REVIEW.md` (2 KB). Decisions final (user, 2026-10-18). Runs as Stream B in its own git worktree, in parallel with P302 (user override of one-phase-at-a-time; zero file overlap: P303 touches docs and the docs tool only, P302 touches ADE tests and components). Same pipeline as P299 (`ingest_files` distill on plain text, sequential, with the P298 prompts), split by section since the input cap is 120,000 characters per call. Structure matters even for the small files: one plan covers all three, with per-file output shape, section ids, and a pointer scheme so code comments and docs that cite `ARCHITECTURE.md §n` still resolve. The original text stays in git and is referenced by `git show <commit>:<path>` where a pointer needs it. Planner decides and states: output form (replace in place vs side-by-side), how exact technical details (error strings, limits, identifiers, numbers, file paths) are kept or verified (e.g. `internal/textloss` loss counts per section, a hand-read sample, a no-lost-open-item check for ARCHITECTURE's Known open items), what is kept verbatim (tables only as one headline figure per the distill rules; known open items entry text), cost from the P299 mean, and the reference repoint.

title: Code review (one Opus round, all three dimensions) of code changes only. Decisions final (user, 2026-10-18). Scope: everything changed since the last review session (the reviewer finds the base in git per CLAUDE.md and states it), minus all documentation: nothing under `docs/`, no `*.md`, no plan, spec, HISTORY.md or pending-changes files. Code, tests, scripts, prompts, configs and workflows-as-patches count. Findings file `plans/P301-findings.md` committed before any fixer starts, then one sequential Sonnet fixer commits per group of related findings; a round finding nothing real says so.
lines: The P301 code review is a single Opus round covering all three dimensions, and it reviews code changes only.
P301 review scope is everything changed since the last review session; the reviewer finds the base in git per CLAUDE.md and states it.
P301 review scope excludes all documentation: nothing under docs/, no *.md, no plan, spec, HISTORY.md or pending-changes files.
P301 review scope includes code, tests, scripts, prompts, configs and workflows-as-patches.
In P301 the findings file plans/P301-findings.md must be committed before any fixer starts; then one sequential Sonnet fixer commits per group of related findings.
A review round that finds nothing real must say so.
P301 fixed 7 findings (1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 4.1, 4.2) and skipped none.
The fix for finding 3.1 ships as the unapplied pending patch docs/pending-changes/.github__workflows__pr.yml.patch, to be applied from an environment with workflow scope.
